items.title: nixlbench: validate --op_type argument
items.body:
## What?

Validate the `--op_type` argument at config parse time. Only `READ` and `WRITE` are accepted; any other value now exits with an error:

    Invalid op type: REA. Must be one of [READ, WRITE]

## Why?

An invalid `--op_type` value (for example a typo like `REA`) is silently treated as WRITE, since the only check performed downstream is:

    nixl_xfer_op_t xfer_op = XFERBENCH_OP_READ == xferBenchConfig::op_type ? NIXL_READ : NIXL_WRITE;

I hit this while benchmarking GDS. A typo produced a full result table that looked like a READ run (the config banner prints `Op type : REA` as given), but it was actually running WRITE, which invalidated a READ vs WRITE comparison until I noticed.

It also affects `--check_consistency`: an invalid value matches neither the READ nor the WRITE branch in `validateTransfer()`, so the consistency check is silently skipped.

## How?

Added the check right after parsing in `xferBenchConfig::loadParams()`, following the existing validation pattern used for `--posix_api_type`.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Added validation for transfer operation types.
  * Invalid values now produce an error and prevent benchmark configuration from loading.

items.body:
Maintenance round, 2026-08-13. Repo-level files only, so no version bump is due.

## FUTURE-IDEAS.md → the tracker

Each parked idea was assessed one by one and moved to its own issue, labelled `enhancement` + `low-priority` (QEP-2 label names, created here ahead of the meta#358 rollout so `labels sync` will conform rather than collide). The issue bodies carry the original evidence plus a dated merit assessment, so deleting the file loses nothing:

| Idea | Issue | Assessment in brief |
|---|---|---|
| mirror-lecture | #36 | Strongest candidate — highest measured frequency, stable playbook |
| triage-build | #37 | Real, but coordinate with meta#304's jupyter-book-fixer first |
| migrate-rng | #38 | Time-limited; settle the rng convention in the manual first |
| intake-lecture | #39 | Real but bursty; build at the start of the next intake batch |
| migrate-data | #40 | Fully specified playbook, low volume; wait for a scheduled tranche |
| editorial-round | #41 | Conditional on a gap remaining after check-style ships (#3) |
| benchmarking-programme consumers | #42 | Telemetry reader is actionable now; the other two are blocked upstream |
| naming convention | #43 | Absorbed by the namespace-consolidation proposal |

The file's **Rejected** list is preserved here for the record: per-measurement skills (`cold-start`, `sweep-bench`, `scaling-curve`) are measurements rather than workflows and live as scripts inside the benchmark plugin; typo/grammar skills are too trivial to need a skill; `track-runtime` is workstream C's job (see #42).

All references to the file (README, AGENTS, CATALOG, developing-skills, myst.yml) now point at the [label query](https://github.com/QuantEcon/skills/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Aenhancement+label%3Alow-priority).

## NEXT-SESSION.md retired

Session state now lives in workplan issues with sub-issues as tasks, per QEP-2 practice — #25 already holds it, revised more recently than the scratch file needed. AGENTS.md states the new convention and the `.gitignore` entry is gone. (The scratch file's remaining unique content — the gotchas — is already in the shipped docs or in #25.)

## README deduplication

README kept restating what other files own: the doc map (AGENTS.md), the repo layout tree (developing-skills § Repo layout), and the validate.py + version-bump details (developing-skills § Versioning and releases, AGENTS § Working in this repo). Those sections are now pointers, and the `qe` blurb no longer implies `check-style` runs — it is merged scaffolding, as CATALOG says. README still owns what the doc map assigns it: what the marketplace is, and installation.

- Generalizes the docstring for `_coerce_data_for_evaluate` in `_benchmarking_dataclasses.py` to accurately reflect its use across all task types, not just forecasting.

No.

A quick sanity check to ensure the updated docstrings accurately reflect the method signatures.

No tests were added as this is strictly a documentation/docstring cleanup. However, all existing benchmarking tests and lint checks pass locally.

items.body:
## Summary

Scaffolding PR for #679. The original OOM root cause (--parallel-algorithm aggressive racing benchmark assemblies against unit tests) is already fixed on main by #723's commit 6e022f58: the main dotnet test pass now always excludes every benchmark test project, and benchmark projects (if any) are run individually afterwards.

## Remaining scope for this PR

In development/buildtest:

1. Fix the flag typos:
   - -b|--no-benchmmarks becomes -b|--no-benchmarks (line 69, plus the matching comment reference at line ~165)
   - -i|--no-integratopn becomes -i|--no-integration (line 73)
2. Fix the still-broken TEST_INTEGRATION assignment (line 74):

   TEST_INTEGRATION=--filter-not-namespace "*.Integration.Tests" --filter-not-namespace "*.Integration.Tests.*"

   This is parsed by sh as an env-var-prefixed command invocation (*.Integration.Tests as a command name), not a simple assignment, so --no-integration/-i is currently a silent no-op. Suggested fix, mirroring the style already used for the (now-fixed) TEST_BENCHMARKS variable and the existing "shellcheck disable=SC2086" on the dotnet test invocation that consumes it unquoted:

   TEST_INTEGRATION="--filter-not-namespace *.Integration.Tests --filter-not-namespace *.Integration.Tests.*"

   No open PR/caller in this repo passes -b/-i today (confirmed via search), so renaming the flags is safe.

Verified: shellcheck development/buildtest is clean both before and after this class of change; no .csproj/.sln in this repo (shell-scripts-only, so no dotnet buildcheck applies).

## Out of scope / needs follow-up

credfeto asked (issue comment, 2026-07-19) whether --parallel-algorithm sequential (and --long-running) could be reintroduced for the per-project benchmark dotnet test invocation, ideally as part of this issue's scope. This can't be verified from within credfeto/scripts itself - there are no benchmark test projects here - and prior direct evidence (#723's issue body, commit a0bf8ee1) showed at least one real benchmark project's test host rejects those flags outright (exit code 5, "Zero tests ran") when run standalone. Recommend validating this against a real benchmark project (e.g. in funfair-server-ethereum) before deciding whether to add it back; flagging here rather than silently narrowing scope.

## Test strategy

- shellcheck development/buildtest after the fix
- Manual inspection that $TEST_INTEGRATION word-splits into exactly the four intended arguments when passed unquoted to dotnet test

Closes #679

items.title: Add RCM40/RCM46 Optimal Power Flow and Penicillin fermentation benchm…
items.body:
…arks

Three non-synthetic benchmarks for the composite-vs-direct comparison, self-contained (no dependency on mobo-highdim's own morbo package):

- benchmark_rcm40.py: RCM40 Optimal Power Flow, a real IEEE 14-bus test system (CEC2021 RWCMOP suite, case 40). 34D, 2 objectives (active/ reactive power loss), raw response is a genuinely bus-decoupled 14-bus power-injection vector from one admittance-matrix solve -- cheap linear algebra, no iterative simulation.
- benchmark_rcm46.py: the same real 14-bus system and design space as RCM40 (case 46), but 4 objectives instead of 2 (fuel cost, voltage deviation added). Also documents a genuine discrepancy: RCM40's second objective has an apparent index slip (I(2) against V(1)) that this benchmark's independently-written analogous term doesn't share, suggesting the RCM40 formula really is a typo upstream.
- benchmark_penicillin.py: fed-batch fermentation (Liang et al. 2021), 7D, 3 objectives. The public implementation only exposes the final [-P, CO2, t_stop] triple; this version checkpoints the full 5-variable state (P, V, X, S, CO2) at 5 fixed steps, exposing real non-monotonic (growth-then-decline) trajectory structure the final-state-only version discards.

All three validated via BenchmarkProblem.validate() and a --quick end-to-end run through run_benchmark() before pushing.

items.title: feat(bench): runBenchmarks — the subset-runnable benchmark matrix unifier
items.body:
## What

`gate.ts` has long referenced *"the bench unifier (`run-benchmarks.ts`)"* — a file that never existed. The 23-adapter registry (`@tangle-network/agent-bench`) could only be run **one benchmark at a time** via `gate-cli`. This adds the missing combinator: the unified, subset-runnable benchmark matrix.

```ts
const report = await runBenchmarks({
  benchmarks: ['humaneval', 'swe-bench'],            // any subset of the 23-adapter registry
  cells: [
    { label: 'opencode/glm-4.6', harness: 'opencode', model: 'glm-4.6', backend: 'sandbox' },
    { label: 'codex/gpt-5',      harness: 'codex',    model: 'gpt-5',   backend: 'sandbox' },
    { label: 'router/flash',     model: 'deepseek-v4-flash',           backend: 'router'  },
  ],
  routerBaseUrl, routerKey, n: 20,
})
console.log(printBenchmarksReport(report))   // leaderboard: resolve-rate + mean score per (benchmark × cell)
```

Runs a **subset of the registry** over a **matrix of agent cells** (harness × model × persona), each scored by the benchmark's **own deterministic judge**, and ranks them. This is the question *"which harness/model/persona wins on which benchmark"* answered over any subset in one call — general enough for any consumer at any level of the stack.

## Built on existing primitives — no new mechanism

- each cell = one `openSandboxRun` shot (the SWE worker's primitive), driven by `resolveBenchClient` (off-box router OR in-box sandbox; **harness rides `sandboxOverrides.backend.type`**)
- deliverable = the adapter's **own** parser (`adapter.output`), default final-text — so the unifier needs **zero per-benchmark branching**
- concurrency = the shared `runPool`
- subset = the `benchmarks` + `cells` arrays plus `n`/`ids`/`split`

## Fail-closed

- unknown benchmark key → throws (typo caught loud)
- benchmark whose `preflight` fails (no Docker/venv/dataset) **or** whose judge rejects its own gold → recorded `unavailable`, **never a silent 0%**
- a thrown shot → `errored`, **excluded from the resolve denominator** so a harness outage can't masquerade as a capability result

## Proof

- `bench/src/run-benchmarks.test.mts` — offline (stub adapter + stub shot): 24-shot matrix expansion, judged aggregation + leaderboard sort, error accounting, `ids`/`reps` subsetting, unavailable-skip, judge self-check, and every fail-loud guard. Passes.
- `examples/benchmark-matrix` — **self-proving**: runs an offline demo with no creds (prints a real leaderboard ranking the cells), or live with `TANGLE_API_KEY`. The registry counterpart to `webcode-matrix`.

## Scope

Additive. Deletes nothing; `gate`/`gate-cli` and every existing eval are untouched (one stale comment in `gate.ts` corrected). New files typecheck and lint clean; the one pre-existing `tsc` error in `bench/src/trata-gepa.mts` is unrelated (present on `main`, a GEPA `SelfImproveOptions` drift).

items.body:
## Summary

Redo of #230 (reverted in #231), this time using the mechanism GitHub actually supports.

The `bench` job had a static 2×4 matrix, so **every** trigger created 8 jobs — and 7 of them
typically gated themselves off in their own first step. Those self-skipping legs still showed up
in the "Running now / queued" panel on the Pages benchmarks page, so the panel advertised work
that would never run.

This moves the selection into a new cheap `plan` job (`ubuntu-latest`, JSON + label arithmetic
only — no VPC access, so it stays off the scarce self-hosted runner). It emits the chosen legs as
JSON, and `bench` consumes them via `strategy.matrix.include: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.matrix) }}`.
A skipped leg now never becomes a job at all — so the site needs **no** gate-decision logic of its
own and cannot drift out of sync with the workflow. One source of truth, which was the goal.

The internal `Gate` step and the six `if: steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true'` guards are gone: every
leg that exists is a leg that should run.

### Why not #230's approach

#230 put the per-leg decision directly in `bench`'s job-level `if:`, referencing `matrix.tier` /
`matrix.bench`. The `matrix` context **is not available** in `jobs.<id>.if` (only
`github`/`inputs`/`needs`/`vars` are), so the file became an invalid workflow and every push failed
validation with zero jobs created. `needs` *is* available in both `if:` and `strategy` — hence a
preceding job that publishes the list.

## Behaviour

Unchanged. The planner reproduces the old shell gate exactly: `workflow_dispatch` `tier`/`benchmark`
inputs, and PR `benchmark-<tier>` / `benchmark-<tier>-<bench>` exact-match labels. The collaborator
trust guard now sits on `plan`, which `bench` inherits transitively via `needs` — so an untrusted PR
never even reaches the planner.

Two small hardening changes fall out of the rewrite:
- Label matching goes through `toJSON` instead of a `','`-join, so label names containing commas
  can no longer smear into a false match.
- `bench` keys off a `has_legs` output rather than introspecting the JSON, covering the corner case
  where the coarse label check passes but no leg matches exactly (e.g. a `benchmark-smoke-typo`
  label) — which would otherwise be an empty-matrix error rather than a clean skip.

## Test plan

`#230` passed a YAML parse and a logic dry-run and still broke production, so this round adds the
two checks that would actually have caught it.

- [x] **actionlint** — added `.github/actionlint.yaml` declaring the self-hosted `ibm-vpc` label.
      Confirmed it reproduces the #230 breakage verbatim on that commit
      (`context "matrix" is not allowed here. available contexts are "github", "inputs", "needs", "vars"`).
      On this branch it reports **1** finding — identical to the pre-existing baseline on `main`
      (a `github.head_ref` warning in the runmeta step, untouched here). No new findings.
- [x] **Gate parity, 16 scenarios** — extracted the planner *from the workflow YAML* (not retyped)
      and diffed its selected legs against a reference model of the old shell gate across all
      dispatch/PR permutations, including outside-contributor and first-timer rejection,
      comma-in-label-name, and coarse-pass-but-no-exact-match. All 16 match leg-for-leg.
- [x] **Real GitHub Actions probe** — because actionlint is not GitHub. A throwaway push-triggered
      workflow (ubuntu-latest, no secrets, no spend) exercised the exact mechanism and confirmed:
      the dynamic matrix expands into correctly-named legs (`smoke / tau2`, `full / spreadsheetbench`);
      matrix-derived `env` resolves (`TIER=smoke ITERATIONS=3` / `TIER=full ITERATIONS=10`, i.e. the
      `matrix.tier == 'smoke' && '3' || '10'` pattern the real workflow depends on);
      an empty selection **skips** rather than erroring; and an `aggregate`-style `needs` +
      `if: always()` job still runs when its dependency skipped. The probe was removed before
      opening this PR — the diff is the workflow plus the actionlint config.
- [x] GitHub raised no workflow-file validation failure for this branch's pushes (the check #230 failed).
- [ ] After merge: add a `benchmark-smoke-tau2` label to a PR and confirm the queue panel lists
      exactly one leg instead of one live plus seven skipped.

items.title: docs(bench): measure English WER for the GigaAM Multilingual CTC heads
items.body:
## Summary

Measures **English** WER for the two GigaAM Multilingual charwise-CTC heads (`ml_ctc` 220M,
`ml_ctc_large` 600M) on a 1000-sample seed-42 slice of **LibriSpeech `test-clean`** — the
standard clean-English ASR benchmark (public, CC BY 4.0). Follow-up to #151 (Russian WER).

## Results (verbatim WER %, 95% CI)

| Head | English (LibriSpeech test-clean) | *Russian clean (ref, #151)* |
|---|---|---|
| `ml_ctc_large` (600M) | **4.63 (4.4–5.1)** | 4.44 |
| `ml_ctc` (220M) | 6.67 (6.4–7.3) | 6.15 |
| `rnnt` (Russian-only) | **100** | 3.55 |

**Reading:** the 600M head on English (4.63%) is only ~0.2 pp behind its own Russian
clean-read WER — the model card's "moderate on English" understates it on clean read. The
Russian-specialized `rnnt` / `e2e_rnnt` heads have a **Cyrillic-only** vocabulary and cannot
produce English at all (100%), so the Multilingual heads are the only option for English.

**Metric:** verbatim WER — the Russian words-to-digits ITN / anglicism normalization used in
the Russian table does not apply to English (normalized vs verbatim agree to within 0.2 pp).

## Not measured
- **Kazakh / Kyrgyz / Uzbek** — no reference set on hand. Common Voice 16.1 was removed from
  the Hub (its old `mozilla-foundation/common_voice_16_1` id 404s), so the CV route is dead.

## Changes
- `scripts/prepare_librispeech.py` — downloads LibriSpeech test-clean and builds a manifest
  pointing at the FLAC files directly (gigastt decodes FLAC via symphonia; no conversion).
- Commit the manifest + three result artifacts; add a docs section + CHANGELOG entry.
- Exclude `benchmark/manifests/` + `benchmark/results_full/` from `typos` (ASR reference /
  hypothesis transcripts are data — dialect spellings like "nothin" / "answerd" are not typos).

## Reproduce
```
python scripts/prepare_librispeech.py
cd benchmark
python benchmark.py --runners gigastt_ml_ctc       --dataset librispeech_test_clean --max-samples 0 --no-cache
python benchmark.py --runners gigastt_ml_ctc_large --dataset librispeech_test_clean --max-samples 0 --no-cache
```

items.title: fix: CLI defects where a failed call read as a clean result, and unfalsifiable benchmark cases
items.body:
Acting on what the six validation reviews found. Every defect was reproduced by execution before being fixed, and every fix verified in both directions — a fix that only makes things stricter is easy to get wrong the other way.

## Three CLI defects: a failed call reading as success

| Defect | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `history record` applied partially | Wrote the dir + `report.md`, **then** parsed `--scores-json`. A malformed brace threw in between, leaving a review `history list` cannot see (no `metadata.json`), and a fresh timestamp per retry meant orphans accumulated | Both JSON args parsed before anything touches disk |
| `history clean` deleted unprompted | Whole surface was `--dir` and `--keep`; `--keep` defaulted to 20, so a bare call removed however many reviews existed past 20 — a count the caller never saw — in a usually-untracked directory | Names every review it would remove, `--dry-run`, and `--confirm-delete N` that must match |
| Mistyped filter → exit 0 | `freshness --pack no/such --fail-on expired` exited 0, so a typo made a CI gate that could never fire. Same for `rules run --rule <typo>` and `benchmark run --case <typo>` | Each names the unmatched identifier and points at the listing command |

The first one matters most in practice: that JSON is assembled **by an LLM** following `skills/akos-review`, so a malformed brace is the expected failure mode, not an edge case.

Also fixed a lying label I introduced while fixing the second: the preview loop printed `removing:` on a call that then refused.

## Two benchmark cases that could not fail

Both Level C cases passed **with the fixture deleted entirely**. Their `must_mention` phrases sat in their own `prompt`, the mock matches triggers against the whole prompt and echoes them back, and the assertion checked that echo.

The M8 "fix" that made canned responses repeat their triggers verbatim is what closed the loop it was meant to open.

The fixtures already carried the signal, so the fix is to stop the prompt carrying it too. `tests/unit/test_benchmark_cases.py` asserts the *property*, not the symptom: every Level C case must fail without its fixture, and no `must_mention` phrase may appear in its own prompt. **Confirmed the guard works by reinstating the old prompt and watching both tests go red**, then restoring.

## Two pack examples corrected in place

Not quietly rewritten — the miscalibration is the more useful lesson.

- **`tool-design` 1.1.0** — `examples.md` called `history clean`'s missing dry-run "a soft finding rather than a defect", granting the TDE51 exemption for commands whose scope is fixed by their arguments. `--keep 20` made the real scope unseen state: the ★ safety-floor CRITICAL row. A worked example that under-applies its own rules teaches under-application.
- **`coding-agents` 1.1.0** — `examples.md` held up commit `4c3e854` as its honesty exemplar on one candid sentence. Four lines earlier the same message claims `python3 rules/runner.py list` "was already exercised" — that subcommand does not exist. Both facts now stand together, because the honest sentence is what made the unverified one read as trustworthy.

## Test plan

```
doctor.sh                exit 0   60 checks
validate.py all          exit 0   76 files
freshness.py             exit 0   54 fresh
benchmark run            exit 0   21 pass
unit tests               exit 0   98 OK   (was 82)
4 integration scripts    exit 0   all pass
```

Sabotage-verified, not assumed: reinstating the leaky Level C prompt makes the new guard fail with a message naming the cause; restoring makes it pass.

## Deliberately not fixed here

`rules/security/secret-in-source.py` applies `is_fixture_or_doc_path` only to its generic branch, so the vendor-pattern and JWT branches flag AKOS's own benchmark fixtures — `akos rules run .` exits 2 on this repo. That is arguably correct (a real `service_role` JWT is a secret wherever it lives) and needs its own decision, not an opportunistic edit in a diff that claims to do something else.

Still open from the reviews and recorded in the CHANGELOG rather than carried quietly: no data-vs-instruction boundary for reviewed content; `history record` copies reports verbatim with no redaction; `rules/` wired to no agent; `backend-reviewer` unrouted; five agents hardcoding `pau-avila`.

items.title: Import benchmark init from CommonSolve
items.body:
## What changed and why

Import `init` directly from its owner, CommonSolve, in the benchmark script. AirspeedVelocity runs the script in a temporary project, so the workflow adds CommonSolve as a direct benchmark dependency.

This restores the benchmark workflow after OrdinaryDiffEqDefault 2.4.3 stopped blanket-reexporting its dependencies. A transitive CommonSolve install is not loadable from an isolated benchmark project, so the workflow must declare it explicitly.

CommonSolve is already a ModelingToolkit dependency and uses the MIT license.

Closes https://github.com/SciML/ModelingToolkit.jl/issues/4910.

## Verification

Failing before, using Julia 1.12.6 and an isolated AirspeedVelocity-shaped local project (including CommonSolve as a direct dependency) while loading the unfixed script from `master`:

```console
$ env JULIA_LOAD_PATH=@:@stdlib julia +release --startup-file=no --project=.benchmark-repro -e 'source = read(`git show HEAD:benchmark/benchmarks.jl`, String); include_string(Main, source, "benchmark/benchmarks.jl")'
ERROR: LoadError: UndefVarError: `init` not defined
  @ benchmark/benchmarks.jl:60
```

The script change alone also discriminates the workflow change: with CommonSolve omitted from the isolated project, it fails immediately instead of reaching the benchmarks.

```console
$ env JULIA_LOAD_PATH=@:@stdlib julia +release --startup-file=no --project=.benchmark-repro -e 'include("benchmark/benchmarks.jl")'
ERROR: LoadError: ArgumentError: Package CommonSolve not found in current path.
```

Passing after both changes, with CommonSolve added as a direct dependency of the AirspeedVelocity-shaped project:

```console
$ env JULIA_LOAD_PATH=@:@stdlib julia +release --startup-file=no --project=.benchmark-repro -e 'include("benchmark/benchmarks.jl"); println("PASS benchmark suite definitions: ", length(SUITE))'
PASS benchmark suite definitions: 5
$ env JULIA_LOAD_PATH=@:@stdlib julia +lts --startup-file=no --project=.benchmark-repro-lts -e 'include("benchmark/benchmarks.jl"); println("PASS benchmark suite definitions: ", length(SUITE))'
PASS benchmark suite definitions: 5
```

Additional local checks:

```console
$ actionlint .github/workflows/benchmark.yml
$ julia +release --startup-file=no --project=../ModelingToolkit.jl/.runic-env -e 'using Runic; exit(Runic.main(["--check", "benchmark/benchmarks.jl"]))'
$ git diff -- .github/workflows/benchmark.yml benchmark/benchmarks.jl | typos -
$ git diff --check
```

All four commands exited successfully with no output.

The required root QA group was also run against this branch:

```console
$ GROUP=QA JULIA_DEPOT_PATH="$PWD/.registry-depot:/home/crackauc/.julia" julia +release --startup-file=no --project=. -e 'using Pkg; Pkg.test(coverage=false)'
Test Summary:                                  | Pass  Fail  Error  Total      Time
QA                                             |   20     3      2     25  66m15.2s
ERROR: Package ModelingToolkit errored during testing
```

The same failures reproduce on clean upstream `master` and are unrelated to the benchmark files changed here. They are existing JET/ExplicitImports/public-API QA debt tracked separately in https://github.com/SciML/ModelingToolkit.jl/issues/4670.

The full timed AirspeedVelocity benchmark matrix was not run locally. The benchmark suite was loaded through the failing `init(prob)` call on both supported Julia channels, but individual benchmark trials were not executed.

The draft PR's full AirspeedVelocity workflow subsequently passed on both supported channels:

- Julia LTS: success in 29m07s — https://github.com/SciML/ModelingToolkit.jl/actions/runs/31534720796/job/93922977895
- Julia 1: success in 56m14s — https://github.com/SciML/ModelingToolkit.jl/actions/runs/31534720796/job/93922977984

items.title: perf(zenzai): 誤入力訂正のincremental探索を高速化
items.body:
## 概要

`experimentalRequestTypoCorrection` のN-gram探索を、候補・スコアを変えずに高速化します。

azooKeyDesktop相当のgradual入力では、誤入力訂正ステージのp90をDirect／Roman2Kana／AZIKのすべてで20ms未満にしました。通常の `requestCandidates` 経路には変更を加えていません。

## 変更内容

- LM状態をtoken prefix trieとして共有
- InputTableの状態遷移とpending文字列の先頭tokenをキャッシュ
- 同じ有限N-gram履歴から得られる次token分布と派生計算を共有
  - 5-gramでは末尾4tokenが同じ場合だけ共有するため厳密です
- append-onlyなgradual入力で、安全な探索地点から再開するincremental checkpointを追加
  - 新しい末尾文字を参照し得ない地点だけを保存します
  - prompt、入力方式、設定、既存prefixが完全一致しない場合はfull-searchへフォールバックします
- N-gramの語彙走査でtokenに依存しない項をループ外へ移動
- latency、探索hypothesis数、枝刈り数、LM評価回数、LM cache hit/missを出力するbenchmarkを追加
- incremental探索とfull-search、および変更前後の候補完全一致テストを追加

探索幅はazooKeyDesktopの設定である `beamSize=16`、`topK=32`、`nBest=3` のままです。候補を近似する枝刈りやスコア調整は追加していません。

## 性能

M2 Pro、release、azooKeyDesktopの実5-gramモデル、各prefixを1回ずつ伸ばす条件です。

| 入力方式 | 変更前 typo p90 | 変更後 typo average | 変更後 typo p90 | 高速化 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Direct | 42.32ms | 17.42ms | 17.50ms | 約2.4倍 |
| Roman2Kana | 137.87ms | 16.82ms | 17.81ms | 約7.7倍 |
| AZIK | 193.92ms | 17.10ms | 17.79ms | 約10.9倍 |

探索量も削減されています。

| 入力方式 | expanded hypotheses | LM evaluations |
|---|---:|---:|
| Direct | 79,364 → 10,847 | 1,051 → 405 |
| Roman2Kana | 633,400 → 46,769 | 869 → 624 |
| AZIK | 291,313 → 26,665 | 1,342 → 752 |

長文全体を一度だけ渡すone-shot条件でも、fresh converterで5回計測した平均が次のように改善しました。

| 入力方式 | 変更前 | 変更後 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Direct | 180.2ms | 107.3ms |
| Roman2Kana | 307.0ms | 104.7ms |
| AZIK | 380.8ms | 120.5ms |

one-shotではincremental checkpointは利用されないため、有限履歴分布・token prefix・InputTable遷移などの共有による改善です。

通常gradual変換単体はhot pathを変更しておらず、同条件の交互計測でも平均は同等でした。誤入力訂正を合わせた合計時間ではなく、benchmarkは通常変換とtypo探索を分けてreportします。

## 動作不変の検証

変更前の `f874ff0` と変更後について、Direct／Roman2Kana／AZIKの全233 prefixで以下をhash化しました。

- 候補数と候補順
- `correctedInput`
- `convertedText`
- `score`、`lmScore`、`channelCost`、`prominence` のFloat bit pattern

両者とも指紋は `cf821d320b7e9574` で完全一致しました。

また、incremental checkpointを使う探索と毎回full-searchする探索を3入力方式で直接比較し、`[ZenzaiTypoCandidate]` の完全一致を確認しています。

## 検証

- `xcrun swift test -c release --traits Zenzai --filter ZenzaiTypoFingerprintTests/testGradualNGramCandidateFingerprint`
- `xcrun swift test -c release --traits Zenzai --filter ZenzaiTypoIncrementalTests/testIncrementalCheckpointMatchesFullSearchExactly`
- 実N-gram gradual typo benchmark
- 標準release全テスト: 180件中179件成功
  - `testKimiAndThenDelete` の1件は変更前のbaseでも同じく再現する既存失敗です

items.title: Bake Sunspot into issuer image + align settlement timestamp to epoch
items.body:
## Summary

Eight atomic commits in two unrelated tracks:

**Issuer image runtime + build hygiene**
- `Add .dockerignore` — bound the new repo-root build context (excludes `**/target/`, `node_modules/`, etc; whitelists `circuits/target/zksettle_slice.{json,ccs,pk}`).
- `Add .railwayignore` — equivalent exclusions for Railway uploads.
- `Move backend image build context to repo root` — flips all three services in `docker-compose.yml` plus the e2e compose to `context: .` / `dockerfile: backend/Dockerfile` and rewrites Dockerfile COPY paths.
- `Bake Sunspot CLI and circuit artefacts into backend image` — adds a `sunspot-builder` stage pinned to the same rev as the `gnark-verifier-solana` Cargo dep, plus the three artefacts under `/artefacts` and the `SUNSPOT_*` env wiring on `issuer-service`. The artefacts (~9 MB total) are now tracked under `circuits/target/`.
- `Add CORS allowed origins env to api-gateway` — defaults to `http://localhost:3000` so a fresh `docker compose up` is browser-usable.

**Solana program correctness**
- `Derive settlement timestamp from epoch boundary` — `verify_proof::handler` and the `settle_hook` transfer hook were passing `clock.unix_timestamp` straight into `verify_bundle`, which only matches the witness at the instant an epoch flips. Both now recompute `epoch * EPOCH_LEN_SECS`. Test fixture + `TimestampMismatch` error message updated to match.

**Frontend devnet hardening**

### Phase 1 — Research (basis for changes)

**GitHub (2026 guides / docs):** ranking blends text relevance (repo name, About description, topics, README) with popularity/freshness (stars, forks, recent activity). items.title: AG-17660 allow narrowing PR benchmarks to specific examples
items.body:
## What

CI supports `/benchmarks` on a PR to compare the head against its base. This adds the ability to **narrow the run to specific examples**:

```
/benchmarks simple-sparkline
/benchmarks simple-sparkline simple-chart
```

A bare `/benchmarks` (and every non-comment trigger — schedule, push, workflow_dispatch) still runs the full example set, so existing behaviour is unchanged.

## How

- **`tools/benchmark/benchmark-examples.js`** — new `resolveExamples()` is the single source of truth for resolving + validating a requested subset (empty request → all runnable examples; unknown names throw). It's threaded through `shardExamples()` and a new CLI `--examples` flag, which accepts names separated by commas and/or whitespace so the comment body can be forwarded verbatim.
- **`tools/benchmark/browser-benchmark.ts`** — its existing `--examples` filtering now routes through the shared `resolveExamples()`, removing a duplicated validate-and-filter block.
- **`.github/workflows/benchmark.yml`** — the *Compute shard matrix* step parses the `/benchmarks [name...]` comment body and forwards the requested names. The comment body is read via `env:` (never interpolated into the `run:` script) to avoid shell injection from untrusted comment text. An unknown example name fails `benchmark-examples.js`, so a typo fails the resolve job loudly rather than silently benchmarking the wrong subset.
- **`tools/benchmark/benchmark-examples.test.js`** — new `node:test` unit tests covering parse / resolve / shard, matching the zero-dependency convention of the sibling `contention.test.ts`.

Narrowing reduces the shard matrix to only the requested examples (e.g. one example → a single shard), and the report job's per-run shard-count integrity check derives its expected count from the same matrix, so it stays consistent.

## Verification

- `node --test tools/benchmark/benchmark-examples.test.js` — 5/5 pass
- CLI checked for narrow / bare / unknown inputs (unknown exits non-zero with an `Available:` list)
- Simulated the workflow's bash parse across bare `/benchmarks`, single/multiple names, multiline bodies, and bad names

items.title: Catalog fixes, test suite, sitemap and a lighter client bundle
items.body:
Follow-up to #17, which merged before this commit was pushed. Six improvements picked from a survey of the codebase.

## Two catalog errors

**`kimi-k2` was a stale copy of `kimi-k2-thinking`** — same name, release month, 1000B params, 262144 context and $0.6/$2.5 pricing, differing only by a few points of score. The catalog claimed 101 models while holding 100, and both entries appeared in every leaderboard and the browse table.

Kimi K2 and K2 Thinking are genuinely different models, so deleting would have been wrong too. The entry becomes **Kimi K2 Instruct**, the real July 2025 non-thinking release — MMLU-Pro 81, GPQA 75, AIME 50, 131K context, `reasoning: false` — which also keeps any shared `/models/kimi-k2` link working.

**Claude Opus 5's SWE-bench Verified was 80**, from before its release notes. It is **96**, corroborated across several sources and consistent with Fable 5 already at 95.

### One suspected error that wasn't

Gemini 3.6 Flash's MMLU-Pro of 47 beside a GPQA of 93 looked like a digit slip. It is not — an independent tracker reports 47.1 and 92.8. Left alone.

## A test suite

The capability index was wrong three times while it was being built: averaging raw scores inverted it, saturated benchmarks then outranked frontier ones, and a model with one published result led the catalog. Each was caught by eye. There are now **25 tests** (`npm test`, vitest):

- the arithmetic — `normalize` clamping and endpoints, category averaging, equal category weighting, the thin-record discount
- **one regression test per failure above**, so the next one is caught by the suite
- integrity checks over `data/models.json` — duplicate ids, duplicate names, unknown benchmark ids, null scores, values outside their benchmark's range

Verified the integrity tests actually bite by mutating the data:

| Mutation | Test that failed |
|---|---|
| Re-add the duplicate name | `has no two models sharing a name` |
| Typo'd benchmark id | `scores only against benchmarks in the registry` |
| Score outside its range | `keeps every published score inside its range` |

## Sitemap and robots

Generated at build — 106 URLs (5 routes + 101 model pages), absolute against `https://gurunave.github.io/llmcompare`, with the origin read from the same environment the deploy workflow already sets so it survives the Pages basePath. Verified against a `GITHUB_PAGES=true` build.

## A lighter client bundle

Architecture blocks move to `data/arch.json`. Only the hardware page sizes weights and a KV cache, but every page that touched the catalog was shipping them — about a fifth of its bytes — to render a price and a benchmark score.

- Shared catalog chunk: **70KB → 59KB**
- `arch` now appears only in the hardware page's own chunk

Confirmed in a browser that the hardware page still sizes correctly — "66 open-weight models fit", GB figures rendering, no page errors — and that `/models/kimi-k2` now renders as Kimi K2 Instruct.

items.title: DNS hygiene: retire iSCSI benchmark hosts, add missing infrastructure records, fix zone typo and broken reverse zone
items.body:
## Summary
Three related fixes to `config/dns_records.csv`, in dependency order — the third explains why the first two were needed.

### 1. Remove 8 retired iSCSI benchmark VMs + 6 profiles
`ubuntu-2404-iscsi-bench-01..05` and `benchmark-iscsi-01-01/-02-02/-03-03`, plus `ubuntu-2404-iscsi-bench.yml` and `benchmark-iscsi-1..5.yml`. The benchmark implementation landed in `917fb76` and the run is complete. `benchmark-storage.yml` (prefix `bench-storage`) is unrelated and untouched.

### 2. Add the physical network infrastructure that was missing from DNS
| Host | IP | Device |
|---|---|---|
| `sw-core-01` | `10.10.10.4` | Dell **N3224T-ON** core switch |
| `ap-01` | `10.10.10.6` | EnGenius **EWS377-FIT** access point |

Static records only (no `dhcp_lease` rows), zone `infra.plexplease.com`, PTRs under `10.10.10.in-addr.arpa` to match the hand-written `k3s-01`/`k3s-deadman-01` entries.

### 3. Fix the `infa.plexplease.com` → `infra.plexplease.com` typo
`photon-mcp-01` had the misspelling in **both** its A record and its PTR target, so forward and reverse were consistently wrong together.


### 4. Repoint PTR records to the authoritative reverse zone
Three PTR records (`photon-mcp-01`, `ubuntu-base-01`, `benchmark-storage-01`) were filed under parent zone `10.in-addr.arpa`, **which does not exist on the Technitium server**. Verified against `10.10.10.2`:

| Zone | SOA present |
|---|---|
| `10.10.10.in-addr.arpa` | yes |
| `10.in-addr.arpa` | **no** |

Live reverse lookups confirmed the impact — records on the missing zone simply don't resolve:
```
10.10.10.5   parent 10.in-addr.arpa        ->  *** NO ANSWER ***
10.10.10.3   parent 10.in-addr.arpa        ->  *** NO ANSWER ***
10.10.10.50  parent 10.10.10.in-addr.arpa  ->  k3s-01.infra.plexplease.com.
10.10.10.51  parent 10.10.10.in-addr.arpa  ->  k3s-deadman-01...
```
All 7 PTR records now use `10.10.10.in-addr.arpa`, and forward/reverse agree for every host.

## Why this matters
Two of the removed benchmark records held DHCP **reservations** (VMware MACs, OUI `00:50:56`) for `10.10.10.4` and `10.10.10.6` — the core switch and the AP. Because that physical gear had **no DNS record at all**, the VM allocator had no idea those addresses were taken and handed them out. Adding the infrastructure records closes that blind spot; without it the same collision would recur on the next provisioning run.

Separately, `ubuntu-2404-iscsi-bench-02/03/04/05` were **all assigned `10.10.10.7`** with distinct MACs — an allocator bug that never incremented the address. `config/dns_records.csv` now has zero duplicate DHCP lease IPs.

### 5. Fix the generator itself
Both defects above came from `NetworkService`, and the data fixes alone would have been undone by the next provisioning run:

- **PTR zone** — `append_dns_records()` built the parent as `'.'.join(parts[-3:])` of the reverse pointer, giving `10.in-addr.arpa` for any `10.x` address. `DNSService._calculate_ptr` already had this right, so the logic is now extracted to `dns.calculate_ptr()` and used by both — removing the duplicate implementation that let them disagree.
- **Duplicate addresses** — `get_next_ip()` derived used addresses only from the CSV *on disk*, so a batch run allocating several hosts before writing handed them all the same address. That is exactly how `bench-02/03/04/05` all landed on `10.10.10.7`. Allocations are now tracked in-instance until written.

New `tests/unit/test_network_service_allocation.py` (6 tests) covers both defects plus the CSV/liveness exclusions. Notably the CSV-exclusion test **already passed** — which is why adding `sw-core-01` and `ap-01` in step 2 is a real fix, not cosmetic: those records now make the allocator treat `.4` and `.6` as occupied.

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest tests/unit` → **346 passed** (340 baseline + 6 new regression tests)
- [x] No remaining `iscsi-bench` / `benchmark-iscsi` references in configs
- [x] No duplicate DHCP lease IPs; no `infa.` occurrences remain
- [x] All 7 PTR records on `10.10.10.in-addr.arpa`; forward/reverse agree per host
- [ ] CI "Lint & Unit Tests" green

items.title: Fix Read the Docs build: modernize config, drop pyrosm compile
items.body:
## Problem

The Read the Docs build was failing. The RTD configuration had not been touched since 2022 and had rotted on several axes:

- **Deprecated build image** — `build.os: ubuntu-20.04` is deprecated on Read the Docs.
- **pyrosm was being compiled from source.** `docs/requirements.txt` installed `pyrosm`, which is sdist-only on PyPI. Its build pulls in `pyrobuf` (also sdist-only, last released 2020), which fails under modern setuptools build isolation (`'PyrobufDistribution' has no 'dry_run'` — the same reason CI builds with `--no-build-isolation` against conda-provided deps). RTD's default `pip install -r` uses build isolation, so the dependency step died before Sphinx ran.
- **Stale toolchain** — unpinned `jupyter-book` + `nbsphinx` + bare `Sphinx` pulling mutually incompatible versions, plus the dead `ipython-genutils`.
- **Removed conf.py options** — `jupyter_execute_notebooks` (renamed to `nb_execution_mode` in myst-nb 0.14) and `myst_admonition_enable` (removed from myst-parser).

## Approach

Notebooks render from their stored outputs (`execution = off`), so pyrosm never needs to run during the build. The only consumer is the autodoc API reference. So instead of compiling pyrosm, this **mocks its compiled Cython modules** via `autodoc_mock_imports` — autodoc reads docstrings straight from the pure-Python wrappers. No pyrobuf, no compiler, no conda; just the doc toolchain plus the pure-Python deps the wrappers import.

## Changes

- **`.readthedocs.yml`** — `ubuntu-24.04` + Python `3.12`.
- **`docs/requirements.txt`** — MyST-NB toolchain only (`myst-nb`, `sphinx`, `sphinx-book-theme`, `ipython`), version-bounded; dropped `jupyter-book`, `nbsphinx`, `ipython-genutils`, `numpydoc`, `sphinxcontrib.bibtex` (unused) and `pyrosm` itself; added `pandas`/`geopandas`/`shapely` (imported by the wrappers).
- **`docs/conf.py`** — add repo root to `sys.path` + `autodoc_mock_imports` for the 10 compiled modules (plus `pyrosm_proto`, `cykhash`); rename `jupyter_execute_notebooks` → `nb_execution_mode` and `execution_allow_errors` → `nb_execution_allow_errors`; drop `myst_admonition_enable`; sync documented version `0.6.0` → `0.6.2`.

## Validation

Built the docs locally in a clean, pyrosm-free venv with the compiled `.so` moved aside (replicating a fresh RTD checkout where the mocks engage), against Sphinx 8.2 / myst-nb 1.4 / sphinx-book-theme 1.2:

- build succeeded — mocks engaged, nothing compiled
- API reference page fully rendered (`OSM` + 8 methods + `get_data`)
- notebooks rendered from stored outputs
- zero warnings introduced by these changes; the remaining 33 build warnings are pre-existing content issues (broken MyST cross-refs in notebooks, a `.. benchmarking` toctree typo, docutils emphasis nits), which RTD does not fail on

## Summary

Phase 1 of #237 — adds a K8s pod Informer that runs as a **backstop** to
the existing callback path. Solves the two failure modes the callback
flow cannot:

- Pre-start failures (ImagePullBackOff / CrashLoopBackOff / …) — benchmark
  transitions to `failed` within `WAITING_FATAL_GRACE_SEC` (default 60s)
- Silent runner death (pod terminates without `/finish` reaching the API) —
  benchmark transitions to `failed` within `TERMINAL_RECONCILE_GRACE_SEC`
  (default 60s)

Callbacks (`/state`, `/log`, `/finish`) stay as the primary path. Runner
image is unchanged. Zero regression to normal completed/failed flows.

Default `K8S_WATCHER_MODE=off` — operators flip to `backstop` after
updating RBAC per `docs/operations/k8s-rbac.md`.

## Design

Full design spec committed in this PR:
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-25-watch-based-runner-status-design.md`

Key decisions:
- All status writes go through `BenchmarkRepository.updateGuarded()` so
  terminal benchmarks are never overwritten (spec §D5)
- Pure `PodStateReducer` with dense unit coverage of all pod.phase ×
  waiting.reason × benchmark.status combinations
- In-memory timing state (`firstFatalWaitingAt`, `firstTerminalAt`) lives
  on the watcher service; reducer is time-stateless
- StartupReconciler uses `podCache.list()` + label filter (NOT exact-name
  lookup — Job-spawned pods have random suffixes; bug caught in Task 6
  code review)

items.title: Introduce BenchmarkPipeline abstraction for extensible workflow integration
items.body:
This PR introduces a `BenchmarkPipeline` abstraction to extend MBF beyond the existing `Benchmark` execution model and enable support for custom workflow implementations and external framework integrations.

### Changes

- Establish foundation for custom workflow implementations and external framework integrations
- Add `BenchmarkPipeline` base interface to generalize execution beyond standard `Benchmark` workflows
- Refactor `Benchmark` abstraction to support extensible pipeline-based execution
- Enable external frameworks to integrate via unified registry mechanism
- Update registry, runtime layer, storage, CLI, and tests to support pipeline execution model
- Add benchmark run status tracking for pipeline execution lifecycle
- Fix minor typo in `CONTRIBUTING.md`

Closes #49

items.body:
### Motivation

- Expand the typo evaluation suite so the total evaluated typo cases exceed the lemma suite for broader coverage. 
- Produce an updated benchmark assessment capturing results from the expanded typo corpus and the stable lemma pipeline.

### Description

- Add a large extended typo fixture at `test-data/fixtures/typo/typo_tokens_by_error_type.extended.json` containing ~500 token cases for the token-level typo suite. 
- Update `test-data/benchmark-reports/typo-report.json` and `test-data/benchmark-reports/lemma-report.json` with new run summaries, timestamps, top failures and per-category metrics. 
- Add a human-readable assessment document `docs/benchmark-assessment-2026-02-25.md` that records the commands used and summarizes the key benchmark metrics.

### Testing

- Ran the benchmark scripts with `PYTHONPATH=backend python scripts/run-typo-benchmark.py` and `PYTHONPATH=backend python scripts/run-lemma-benchmark.py`, which produced updated JSON reports at `test-data/benchmark-reports/typo-report.json` and `test-data/benchmark-reports/lemma-report.json` respectively.

- Lemma benchmark: lemma accuracy = `459/481 (95.43%)`, coverage `481/481 (100%)`, classification accuracy `387/391 (98.98%)`, robustness `73/75 (97.33%)`, and all lemma targets (`min_lemma_accuracy`, `min_classification_accuracy`, `min_robustness_accuracy`) were met.

items.title: docs(readme): document the sweep command that actually produced results/hash.json (#114)
items.body:
<!-- mirrored-from: jt-mchorse/embedding-model-shootout#pr-116 -->

Source: https://github.com/jt-mchorse/embedding-model-shootout/pull/116

The quickstart told readers to reproduce the benchmark with `--queries 200`. The committed `results/hash.json` carries `n_queries: 50`. Following the README gives recall@5 of **0.560**; `docs/benchmarks.md` and the README prose quoting it both say **0.520**.

The number itself is fine — it's real and re-derivable. Re-running with `--queries 50 --seed 42` reproduces the committed artifact exactly, `ndcg_at_10` matching to all 16 digits. What was missing is that **no documented command produced it.**

**Why three existing snapshot tests couldn't see it.** `test_readme_snapshot.py` locks `results/hash.json`'s cells against the README prose; `test_benchmarks_md_snapshot.py` locks the aggregator's rendering of `results/*.json` into `docs/benchmarks.md` (its own docstring says the numbers are "indirectly locked by test_readme_snapshot.py"). So the chain is README prose ↔ artifact ↔ rendered table — all mutually consistent, with the command that *makes* the artifact outside the loop entirely. Every artifact agreed with every other artifact; none agreed with the documented way to produce them.

**The deeper finding, which changed the fix.** Before building the obvious freshness test (regenerate and compare, the shape `chunking-strategies-lab` uses), I checked whether the corpus is committed. It isn't — D-002 keeps it "reproducible from source" — so the test would have to rebuild it, and the corpus is built from the local interpreter's stdlib docstrings. Measured, identical flags:

| | Python 3.11 | Python 3.14 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `corpus build` chunk_count | 11 108 | 12 010 |
| recall@5 | 0.580 | 0.520 |
| NDCG@10 | 0.48522314127483007 | 0.4486406869414832 |

`results/hash.json` records `n_corpus: 12010`, so it's from a 3.14-era stdlib, and **CI runs 3.11 and 3.12**. A regenerate-and-compare test would fail in CI every run; gating it on the interpreter would make it *always skip*, which is its own known failure mode. So this PR ships the interpreter-independent half.

**What ships**

- The documented command becomes `--queries 50 --seed 42` — the invocation that actually produced the artifact, now self-describing rather than relying on argparse defaults. `--seed` is spelled out because D-005 derives the query set from the corpus at sweep time, making it provenance.
- A stated reproducibility caveat carrying the measured numbers above, rather than a vague warning.
- A lock asserting the README's documented flags match the artifact's recorded metadata (`--queries` ↔ `n_queries`), plus a seed-presence check and an anti-vacuous assertion that the documented `--output` is the file being compared against — otherwise the first two assertions compare the README to a file it doesn't write.

**Explicitly not done.** No committed benchmark number is regenerated. Rewriting a published row to match a typo in a command is a benchmark-integrity call, and the 50-query row is what `docs/benchmarks.md`, the README prose, and `test_readme_snapshot.py` all already carry. The underlying question — D-002's "reproducible from source" premise not holding across interpreters — is filed as **#115** with four options, rather than picked here.

**Verification.** Anti-vacuous: restoring the pre-fix README fails both assertions with the real numbers (`assert 200 == 50`). Full suite 438 passed, `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean. `git diff` over `results/` and `docs/` is empty — nothing regenerated. All probes ran into `/tmp`, including a throwaway Python 3.11 venv for the cross-interpreter measurement.

Closes #114
